column1: # Reviewed exceptions for the dynamic scan of the -Web GUI (.github/workflows/dast.yml).
# zap-baseline.py reads this file: <rule id> TAB <IGNORE|WARN|FAIL> TAB <reason>.
# Every rule not listed here is a WARN, and any WARN or FAIL fails the job, so a
# new alert is reviewed before it is accepted; Testing/TP.RuntimeScans.Tests.ps1
# fails a line whose reason a reviewer could not check.

column3: Suspicious Comments: app.js's own documentation comments contain the words USER, ADMIN, FROM and WHERE as prose. None is a credential, a hidden path or a note about a weakness, and the file is a public asset of the GUI; the rule matches words, not disclosures.

CSP style-src unsafe-inline: the GUI's own pages send style-src 'self' (TP.WebServer.Tests.ps1 pins the template fill). Only the two routes that serve a run's report add 'unsafe-inline', because Publish-TPAssessmentHTML emits inline style attributes that a CSP hash cannot cover; default-src 'none', img-src and connect-src confine what injected CSS could reach to this server and the run's recorded logo origin.
Modern Web Application: informational. The GUI is a script-driven page whose anchors app.js fills in from /api/runs; the rule describes the application's shape, not a weakness.

Non-Storable Content: informational, and the intended state. Every response is Cache-Control: no-store on purpose, because tenant data must not reach the browser's disk cache, so a response the browser may not store is the design, not a finding; TP.WebServer.Tests.ps1 requires the header on every response.

Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy missing: the GUI needs no cross-origin isolation (no SharedArrayBuffer, no high-resolution timers), and require-corp would make the browser refuse the brand logo a report embeds from the practice's CDN, which does not send CORP. Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy same-origin and the CSP already keep other origins from reading or embedding these responses.

HTTP Only Site: the GUI binds to 127.0.0.1 in its own code (Start-TPWebServer) and the request policy refuses any Host but the loopback name and port, so its traffic never leaves the machine. A TLS listener on loopback would need a locally trusted certificate authority on every operator workstation and would protect nothing a network observer can see.
